title: 1. The rational soul is the true informing form of man — not accidental motion, crasis, or Averroist assistance
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss: that same which informs the body plus with it constitutes man in a certain species belonging toward things — but an informing form. such as Averroes (On the soul book 3, chapter 5) thought to be one toward all, in reality separated from all, plus joined to individuals only through images belonging toward phantasy residing in them; — nor an assisting form. that same which Cicero in the first Tusculan Questions thought Aristotle meant by the word entelechy, plus such as the mixture belonging toward the primary qualities, that same which both impious heretics (Carpocrates, Epiphanes, Prodicus, the Cainites plus Antitactae, in Theodoret, book 5 On divine decrees, chapter on man) plus Galen (in the book That the manners belonging toward the soul follow the temperament belonging toward the body, chapters 3 plus 4, plus Epidemic book 6, plus book 3 On affected places) imagined as the form belonging toward man; — i mean a form that same stands as not accidental — such as continuous plus perennial motion. The rational soul stands as the true form belonging toward man. 1.
pass_b_english: 1. The rational soul is the true form of man.

I mean a form that is not accidental — such as continuous and perennial motion, which Cicero in the first Tusculan Questions thought Aristotle meant by the word entelechy, and such as the mixture of the primary qualities, which both impious heretics (Carpocrates, Epiphanes, Prodicus, the Cainites and Antitactae, in Theodoret, book 5 On divine decrees, chapter on man) and Galen (in the book That the manners of the soul follow the temperament of the body, chapters 3 and 4, and Epidemic book 6, and book 3 On affected places) imagined as the form of man;

nor an assisting form, such as Averroes (On the soul book 3, chapter 5) thought to be one for all, in reality separated from all, and joined to individuals only through images of phantasy residing in them;
but an informing form, which informs the body and with it constitutes man in a certain species of things.
source_text: 1. Anima rationalis est vera hominis forma. Formam dico, neque accidentalem, qualis est continuata & perennis motio, quam entelecheian voce Aristoteli intellectam putavit Cicero, 1. Tusc. quaestionum, & qualis est primarum qualitatum crasis, quam hominis formam finxerunt, tam impii haeretici, Carpocrates, Epiphanes, Prodicus, Cajani & Antitactae, apud Theodoretum lib. 5. de divinis decretis, cap. de homine, quam Galenus, libro quod mores animi sequantur temperamentum corporis cap. 3. & 4. & lib. 6. Epid. & lib. 3. de locis affectis: neque assistentem, qualem Averroes lib. 3. de an. cap. 5. putavit unicam esse omnium, re ab omnibus separatam, neque nisi per imagines phantasiae insidesentes singulis conjunctam: sed informantem, quae corpus informet & cum eo hominem in certa specie rerum constituat.
